printed_headline_estimate: OLS linear regression of county share lacking complete plumbing facilities (Table 3, PDF p. 9 / journal p. 313, N = 3143 counties; model R^2 = 0.3423, F(20,3122) = 81.25, p < 0.001): American Indian or Alaskan Native b = 0.10*** (t = 28.54, p < 0.001); White (bivariate check, Abstract R^2 = 0.0462, P < 0.05; Table 3) b = -0.0213745*** (t = -12.38, p = 0.000); Black or African American b = 0.002 (t = -0.90, p = 0.369); Asian b = -0.04** (t = -3.01, p = 0.003); Other Race b = -0.04** (t = -4.30, p < 0.001); Hispanic or Latino b = 0.004 (t = 1.38, p = 0.167); High school graduate b = -0.03** (t = -4.61, p < 0.001); Urbanicity (1-9 rurality scale) b = 0.0005** (t = 3.73, p < 0.001); Median income b = 0.0000000751* (t = 2.38, p = 0.017); Unemployment b = 0.03 (t = 1.91, p = 0.056). Spatial autocorrelation (PDF p. 8 / journal p. 312): Moran's I = 0.016 (z = 15.55, p < 0.00).
publication_year_note: Printed as Du Bois Review, 13:2 (2016) 305-325, © 2016 Hutchins Center for African and African American Research; no separate online-first publication year is printed on the PDF.
rationale: The paper conducts inferential county-level spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I) and OLS linear regressions (N = 3,143 U.S. counties using 2008-2013 ACS and 2013 USDA ERS Urban Influence Codes) on a valid Criterion 4 outcome (percentage of occupied housing units lacking complete plumbing facilities). However, all empirically tested independent variables in the regressions (Table 3, PDF p. 9) are purely demographic, socioeconomic, rurality, and geographic division predictors (racial/ethnic population shares, median household income, unemployment, gender, median age, high school graduation rate, USDA 1-9 urbanicity code, and Census division dummies). No rule-type legal, administrative, municipal-incorporation, reservation-jurisdiction, tenure, zoning, tariff, governance, or ownership exposure (narrow Criterion 2) is quantitatively measured or tested; legal/institutional mechanisms such as California municipal incorporation exclusion, reservation governance, utility zoning ('blue lining'), and Detroit water shutoffs are discussed only qualitatively/anecdotally as motivating context and data limitations (PDF pp. 13-14, 17). Thus, the inferential estimates do not belong to any SWiM legal/institutional family.
